stages.name: Roman
stages.desc: Rome and the Italian allies who stayed loyal

stages.name: Gauls & Ligurians
stages.desc: Tribes outside Roman control, mostly hostile to Rome

stages.name: Contested
stages.desc: Armies in the field, sieges and divided loyalties

stages.name: Defected to Carthage
stages.desc: Cities and peoples that went over to Hannibal or Carthage

stages.name: Carthaginian-held
stages.desc: Held by Hannibal's army or a Carthaginian force

states.name: Valle d'Aosta
timeline: Alpine valleys of the Salassi; one of the passes Hannibal may have used

states.name: Piemonte
timeline: Taurini and Ligurian tribes; Hannibal storms the Taurini's chief town after crossing the Alps

states.name: Lombardia
timeline: New Roman colony at Cremona; the Insubres rise, and Hannibal wins a cavalry clash at the Ticinus
The Romans fall back south; the Insubres send warriors to Hannibal
Mago is defeated by the Romans in the land of the Insubres

states.name: Trentino-Alto Adige
timeline: Alpine tribes beyond Roman reach

states.name: Liguria
timeline: Ligurian tribes, independent and hostile to Rome
Mago lands at Genua with some fourteen thousand men and takes the town
Mago, wounded, is recalled to Africa; his army sails away

states.name: Emilia-Romagna
timeline: The Boii rise against the new Roman colony at Placentia; Hannibal wins at the Trebia
The Boii ambush and destroy a Roman army in the Litana forest
Hasdrubal arrives from the Alps and besieges Placentia in vain
Hasdrubal's army is gone; the Gauls are left on their own

states.name: Marche
timeline: Picenum and the Roman colonists of the Adriatic coast
Hannibal rests his army and horses on the Adriatic coast
Hannibal marches south; Picenum stays loyal
Hasdrubal is defeated and killed at the Metaurus
Rome's northern frontier is secure again

states.name: Veneto
timeline: The Veneti, long-standing allies of Rome against the Gauls

states.name: Friuli-Venezia Giulia
timeline: Carni and Alpine peoples beyond Roman control

states.name: Abruzzo
timeline: Marsi, Paeligni and Vestini, Rome's hill-country allies
Hannibal's army passes through on its way to Apulia; the allies stay loyal

states.name: Molise
timeline: Pentrian Samnites allied to Rome
Hannibal ravages Samnium and winters at Gerunium; Fabius shadows him
The Pentri stay loyal while other Samnites defect

states.name: Apulia
timeline: Daunian and Greek cities allied to Rome
After Cannae, Arpi, Salapia and other Apulian towns go over to Hannibal
Rome retakes Arpi; the region is fought over
Tarentum is betrayed to Hannibal, but the Romans hold its citadel
Fabius retakes Tarentum and sells its people into slavery

states.name: Basilicata
timeline: Lucanians and the Greek cities of the gulf, allied to Rome
Most of the Lucanians go over to Hannibal
Metapontum and Thurii join Hannibal
Lucanian communities begin to surrender to Rome
Hannibal fights the consul Nero at Grumentum while waiting for Hasdrubal
Hannibal withdraws into Bruttium; Lucania returns to Rome

states.name: Calabria
timeline: Bruttians and the Greek cities of Locri, Croton and Rhegium, allied to Rome
The Bruttians defect to Hannibal
Locri opens its harbour: Bomilcar lands Carthage's only reinforcement for Hannibal
Scipio retakes Locri; Hannibal holds out around Croton
Hannibal sails from Croton for Africa

states.name: Campania
timeline: Capua, Neapolis and the rich Campanian plain, allied to Rome
Hannibal ravages the Falernian plain and slips past Fabius
Capua, the second city of Italy, goes over to Hannibal
Rome starves Capua into surrender and executes its leaders

states.name: Lazio
timeline: Rome and the Latin cities, the core of the alliance
Hannibal rides to the walls of Rome to draw its armies from Capua, then withdraws

states.name: Toscana
timeline: Etruscan cities allied to Rome
Hannibal struggles through the flooded Arno marshes and ravages Etruria
Etruria stays loyal, though Rome keeps watch on Arretium
Etruscan towns supply timber, grain and iron for Scipio's fleet

states.name: Sicily
timeline: A Roman province in the west; Syracuse under King Hiero, Rome's ally
After Hiero's death, Syracuse breaks with Rome and joins Carthage
Marcellus besieges Syracuse; Himilco lands a Carthaginian army in the south
Plague destroys Himilco's army; Syracuse falls and is sacked
Agrigentum falls; all of Sicily is Roman

states.name: Sardegna
timeline: A Roman province, taken from Carthage in 238
Sardinians under Hampsicora revolt; a Carthaginian army lands and is crushed by Torquatus
The revolt is over; Sardinia ships grain to Rome
Roman ships capture Carthaginian transports off the island

states.name: Umbria
timeline: Umbrian towns allied to Rome
Lake Trasimene: Flaminius and fifteen thousand Romans are killed in an ambush
Umbria stays loyal; Spoletium had shut its gates on Hannibal

events.title: Rome declares war
events.text: Roman envoys in Carthage's senate offer peace or war over Saguntum; the senators accept war.

events.title: Malta taken
events.text: The consul Sempronius seizes Carthaginian Malta on his way to attack Africa.

events.title: Crossing the Rhône
events.text: Hannibal ferries his army and thirty-seven elephants across the Rhône.

events.title: Over the Alps
events.text: Hannibal reaches Italy with perhaps twenty-six thousand men, half the army he set out with.

events.title: Scipio lands in Spain
events.text: Gnaeus Scipio lands at Emporion with an army and a fleet, to cut Hannibal off from his base.

events.title: Battle of Cissa
events.text: Gnaeus Scipio defeats Hanno north of the Ebro and takes Hannibal's baggage.

events.title: Battle of the Ticinus
events.text: Hannibal's Numidian horse rout the Roman cavalry; the consul Scipio is wounded.

events.title: Battle of the Trebia
events.text: Hannibal destroys a Roman army in the snow; the Gauls flock to him.

events.title: Ebro naval battle
events.text: Gnaeus Scipio surprises Hasdrubal's fleet at the Ebro mouth and takes twenty-five ships.

events.title: Lake Trasimene
events.text: Hannibal ambushes the consul Flaminius's army in the morning mist; Flaminius is killed.

events.title: A fleet off Pisae
events.text: Seventy Carthaginian ships sail for Italy hoping to meet Hannibal, then turn back before a Roman fleet.

events.title: Fabius the Delayer
events.text: The dictator Fabius shadows Hannibal and refuses battle; Hannibal winters at Gerunium.

events.title: Cannae
events.text: Hannibal encircles and destroys a Roman army of some eighty thousand in an afternoon.

events.title: Capua defects
events.text: Italy's second city goes over to Hannibal, followed by much of the south.

events.title: Mago's gold rings
events.text: Mago pours the rings of dead Romans before Carthage's senate; Hanno asks why a victor needs help.

events.title: Bomilcar at Locri
events.text: Carthage's only reinforcement for Hannibal lands: Numidian horsemen, elephants, money and grain.

events.title: Defeat at Dertosa
events.text: The Scipios beat Hasdrubal at the Ebro; the army voted for Italy is sent to Spain instead.

events.title: Sardinian revolt fails
events.text: Hasdrubal the Bald's army and the rebel Hampsicora are crushed near Cornus.

events.title: Pact with Macedon
events.text: Hannibal allies with Philip V; a Roman fleet at Brundisium keeps Philip out of Italy.

events.title: Syracuse breaks away
events.text: After old Hiero's death, Syracuse turns against Rome and asks Carthage for help.

events.title: Himilco lands in Sicily
events.text: A Carthaginian army of some twenty-eight thousand lands at Heraclea Minoa to save Syracuse.

events.title: Tarentum betrayed
events.text: Young Tarentines open the gates to Hannibal at night; the Romans keep the citadel and the harbour mouth.

events.title: Bomilcar turns back
events.text: Bomilcar's fleet of over a hundred ships sails for Syracuse, sees the Roman fleet off Cape Pachynus, and turns away.

events.title: Syracuse falls
events.text: Marcellus storms Syracuse; Archimedes is killed in the sack.

events.title: The Scipios killed
events.text: Both Scipio brothers are defeated and killed in southern Spain, deserted by their Celtiberian allies.

events.title: Hannibal at the gates
events.text: To save Capua, Hannibal marches on Rome; the city does not stir and Capua falls.

events.title: Capua falls
events.text: Starved out, Capua surrenders; its leaders are executed and its land confiscated.

events.title: Agrigentum falls
events.text: The last Carthaginian stronghold in Sicily is betrayed to the Romans.

events.title: New Carthage taken
events.text: The young Publius Scipio storms Carthage's capital in Spain, with its silver and its fleet base.

events.title: Tarentum retaken
events.text: Fabius retakes Tarentum; Hannibal loses his best port in Italy.

events.title: Battle of Baecula
events.text: Scipio defeats Hasdrubal, who slips away north with his army and treasury to march for Italy.

events.title: Marcellus killed
events.text: Rome's boldest general dies in an ambush near Venusia.

events.title: Hasdrubal over the Alps
events.text: Hannibal's brother crosses the Alps with a second army and lays siege to Placentia.

events.title: Grumentum
events.text: Hannibal fights the consul Nero in Lucania; captured letters reveal Hasdrubal's route.

events.title: Battle of the Metaurus
events.text: Nero marches north to join his colleague; Hasdrubal's army is destroyed and he is killed.

events.title: Battle of Ilipa
events.text: Scipio wins the decisive battle for Spain; Carthage's armies there dissolve.

events.title: Gades lost
events.text: Mago sails from Gades, the last Carthaginian city in Spain, which then goes over to Rome.

events.title: Mago lands at Genua
events.text: Mago sails from Minorca with some fourteen thousand men and takes Genua.

events.title: Convoy lost
events.text: Roman ships capture about eighty Carthaginian transports off Sardinia, reportedly bound for Hannibal.

events.title: Locri retaken
events.text: Scipio retakes Locri; Hannibal holds only the toe of Italy.

events.title: Scipio lands in Africa
events.text: Scipio sails from Sicily and lands near Utica; the war moves to Carthage's door.

events.title: Battle of the Great Plains
events.text: Scipio and Masinissa crush a new Carthaginian and Numidian army.

events.title: Mago defeated
events.text: Mago is beaten and wounded in the land of the Insubres; recalled, he dies at sea.

events.title: Hannibal recalled
events.text: Hannibal sails from Croton for Africa after fifteen years in Italy.

chartNote: Share of the area of present-day Italy, by who mainly held each of today's twenty regions; ancient peoples and cities did not follow these boundaries, and loyalties were often city by city. Spain and Africa, where most of Carthage's forces went, are shown by events, not colours.
